findings.description: Static AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the Lambda function's environment variables, making them readable by anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration permission and committing them to version control.

The function's environment variables are not encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key (no kms_key_arn set), so the sensitive values fall back to the default service key with no explicit key policy, rotation, or audit control.
The function uses nodejs12.x, a deprecated Lambda runtime that no longer receives security patches while continuing to execute code.
No vpc_config block is defined, so the function runs outside any VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group or subnet controls on egress, providing a data exfiltration path.
No code_signing_config_arn is attached, so the deployment package signature is never validated and tampering between build and deployment would go undetected.
The Lambda execution role is created without a permissions_boundary, so there is no guardrail limiting the maximum permissions that can later be attached to this role.
